history.description: Cyrus Mason established the first homestead in the township on Section 31, drawing pioneers from Kentucky, Indiana, and North Carolina.
The village was platted as Edinburg by George Monical, later renamed Georgetown. The name 'Bible Grove' originated from a local legend where hunters discovered a Bible in a nearby grove of trees.
The Bible Grove Christian Church was organized with 37 charter members, on land deeded by early resident Henry Brooks.
The community's post office, which had served the area since 1854, officially closed on October 22, 1988.
Bible Grove remains a quiet, historic unincorporated community in Clay County, serving as the center of Bible Grove Township.
